questions.stem: Immunoglobulin G (IgG) is:
questions.option_b: Produced when an antigen is encountered for the first time
questions.option_c: Responsible for defence against invasion of micro-organisms through the body's mucous membranes
questions.rationale: IgG is the most abundant serum immunoglobulin and the principal antibody of the secondary (memory) immune response; it is produced in large quantities on re-exposure to an antigen and confers long-lasting immunity. It also crosses the placenta to provide passive neonatal immunity. IgM is the dominant antibody of the primary (first-exposure) response. IgA protects mucous membrane surfaces. IgE mediates immediate (Type I) hypersensitivity/allergic reactions. Ref: Microbiology and Immunology — NCK BScN curriculum.

questions.stem: A patient on mechanical ventilation has a high-pressure alarm sounding. The nurse should first:
questions.option_b: Assess the patient and check for causes such as secretions, biting the tube, or pneumothorax
questions.option_c: Sedate the patient to reduce airway resistance
questions.option_d: Decrease the respiratory rate on the ventilator
questions.rationale: HIGH-PRESSURE ALARM on a ventilator indicates increased resistance to airflow or decreased lung compliance. Causes: SECRETIONS in the airway (most common — suction), patient BITING the ETT (insert bite block), BRONCHOSPASM (administer bronchodilator), PNEUMOTHORAX (assess breath sounds, prepare for chest drain), coughing/fighting the ventilator, kinked tubing, water in circuit. The nurse should ASSESS THE PATIENT FIRST (airway, breathing, circulation), then systematically check the circuit. Never increase tidal volume when pressure is already high — this risks barotrauma.

questions.stem: The type of breech in which thighs are flexed with legs extended is called:
questions.rationale: Types of breech presentation: FRANK (extended) BREECH — hips flexed, knees EXTENDED, feet up by the head — most common, accounting for ~65% of breech presentations at term; COMPLETE BREECH — hips and knees both flexed ("tailor sitting"); FOOTLING BREECH — one or both feet present below the buttocks (high risk of cord prolapse). The wording in option B describes frank breech.

questions.stem: The purpose of monitoring central venous pressure (CVP) for the critically ill patient is to:
questions.option_a: Help assess the functioning of the left side of the heart
questions.option_c: Estimate the levels of pulmonary pressures in the critically ill
questions.option_d: Help assess functioning of the mitral and tricuspid valves
questions.rationale: CVP, measured in the superior vena cava/right atrium, reflects right-heart preload and intravascular volume status. Its clinical use is to guide fluid resuscitation (low CVP suggests under-filling; rising CVP with fluid challenge suggests adequate filling). It does NOT reliably reflect left-heart function or pulmonary pressures (those need PA catheterisation or echocardiography).

questions.stem: A scale of measurement with an absolute zero include: -*
questions.rationale: The ratio scale is the only measurement scale possessing a true/absolute zero point, allowing meaningful ratios (e.g., weight, height, pulse rate). Interval scales lack an absolute zero (Research & Biostatistics, NCK syllabus).

questions.stem: The appropriate distribution of nutrients for a diabetic patient might be:
questions.rationale: The Kenya national diabetes guidelines and IDF/ADA recommend approximately: 45–65% calories from CARBOHYDRATES (preferably complex/high-fibre, low glycaemic index), 15–20% PROTEIN (0.8–1 g/kg/day), and less than 30% FAT (less than 7% saturated fat). Option B approximates this: 60% carbs, 20% fat, 20% protein. Option C underestimates protein at 10% (insufficient); options A and D have inappropriate excess fat or protein.

questions.stem: An infant at 5 minutes of life has: pulse 95/min, cyanotic hands and feet, some flexion of extremities, irregular breathing. The APGAR score is:
questions.rationale: APGAR assessment: HR <100 = 1, acrocyanosis = 1, some flexion = 1, weak irregular respiratory effort = 1, grimace = 1; total ≈ 7. Interpretation guides neonatal resuscitation decisions (Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols).

questions.stem: The presumptive signs of pregnancy include all EXCEPT:
questions.rationale: Classifying signs as presumptive, probable, or positive is fundamental to midwifery assessment. Fetal heart auscultated by examiner = positive sign. Nurses apply this in diagnosis (Myles Textbook for Midwives).

questions.stem: Which eye condition is characterised by progressive deterioration of the macula, resulting in loss of central vision?
questions.rationale: Wet AMD: anti-VEGF injections (ranibizumab); dry AMD: no proven treatment but AREDS2 supplements may slow progression. BScN nurses teach Amsler grid self-monitoring for metamorphopsia and counsel on low-vision aids (Brunner & Suddarth; ophthalmology EBP).

questions.stem: The following is a symptom of abortive poliomyelitis:
questions.rationale: Abortive polio presents with fever, sore throat, malaise — no CNS involvement (Kenya EPI/communicable disease guidelines).

questions.stem: The mode of action of acyclovir as a drug of choice for herpes virus is:
questions.rationale: Acyclovir selective toxicity depends on viral thymidine kinase activation; resistance occurs when this enzyme is absent. Nurses administer IV acyclovir for severe herpes encephalitis and monitor renal function and hydration (BNF).

questions.stem: When developing health promotion plans with clients, the nurse educator should take the role of:
questions.rationale: The nurse acts as a resource person when developing health promotion plans with clients (health promotion/community health nursing texts).

questions.stem: Mechanical factors involved in labour include:
questions.option_a: General fluid pressure, formation of retraction ring, rupture of membranes
questions.option_b: Rupture of membranes, formation of forewaters, general fluid pressure
questions.option_c: Formation of forewaters, polarity, contraction and retraction ring
questions.option_d: Rupture of membranes, cervical effacement, formation of retraction ring
questions.rationale: Mechanical factors (Myles): rupture of membranes, forewaters, and general fluid pressure assist cervical dilatation and fetal descent. Nurses monitor these during labour assessment.

questions.stem: Which ONE of the following is a clinical feature clinical chorio-amnionitis?
questions.option_d: Maternal pulse of 110 beats per minute
questions.rationale: Clinical chorioamnionitis is characterised by maternal fever (>38°C), maternal tachycardia (>100 bpm), fetal tachycardia, uterine tenderness, and foul-smelling amniotic fluid/vaginal discharge. A maternal pulse of 110 bpm (D) represents tachycardia and IS a valid clinical feature. A temperature of 37.4°C is not febrile (below the 38°C threshold) and a non-tender uterus is the opposite of the expected finding. Foul-smelling vaginal discharge (A) is also a feature, but without uterine tenderness, the pulse criterion (D) is the clearer single correct answer in this context. (Myles Textbook for Midwives; Kenya MOH BEmONC guidelines.)

questions.stem: You are taking vital signs observations on a postpartum client who delivered a healthy newborn 4 hours ago. Her temperature is 100.2° F or 37.9 What is the priority nursing action?
questions.option_a: Increase hydration by encouraging oral fluids.
questions.option_d: Notify the doctor Postpartum fever is defined as a temperature of 38.7 degrees C (101.6 degrees F) or greater for the first 24 hours or greater than 38.0 degrees C (100.4 degrees F) on any two of the first 10 days postpartum.
questions.rationale: A temperature of 37.9C (100.2F) within the first 24 hours postpartum is commonly due to dehydration/exertion and is not defined as puerperal fever (>=38C); the priority is to increase oral fluids and reassess (Myles Textbook for Midwives).

questions.stem: The ectoderm differentiates to form the:-
questions.rationale: Per embryology (Myles), the ectoderm gives rise to the nervous system (central and peripheral), skin, and sensory epithelia; cardiovascular and connective tissues derive from mesoderm and respiratory tract from endoderm.

questions.stem: Which term refers to a raised, solid skin lesion less than 1 centimetre in diameter?
questions.rationale: Papules in acne (comedonal) vs psoriasis (scaly) vs viral warts differ in aetiology and management. BScN nurses apply precise lesion terminology in dermatology referral documentation (Brunner & Suddarth; dermatology assessment).

questions.stem: The following statement regarding the learning process is true:
questions.option_a: Perception is sending the information to the brain via the special senses
questions.option_b: Acquisition refers to storing information in the memory centres
questions.option_c: Transfer refers to using information learnt in practice
questions.option_d: Retention refers to information being recorded in the brain
questions.rationale: Transfer of learning is the application of previously learned knowledge or skills to new or practical situations. Perception is the interpretation of sensory input (not merely sensing); retention is storage in memory; acquisition is gaining the information. Option C correctly describes transfer. Ref: Learning process; nursing education.

questions.stem: In normal labour, the fetal movement that occurs after extension is:
questions.rationale: Restitution realigns the fetal head with the shoulders after the twist of internal rotation; external rotation follows. Nurses must narrate the mechanism to students and recognise deviations (Myles Textbook for Midwives).

questions.stem: The following structures in fetal circulation joins the umbilical cord to the inferior vena cava
questions.rationale: Per Myles Textbook for Midwives, the ductus venosus connects the umbilical vein to the inferior vena cava, allowing oxygenated blood to bypass the fetal liver.

questions.stem: Thembi is primigravida at 39 weeks gestational age. She requested induction of labour because she is a student in one of the universities, in preparation for her examination. On examination:Presentation- cephalic, Fundal height- 40cm, foetal heart rate 148 beats per minute. Before induction, the obstetrician examines her and the findings are as follows: cervix-mid position; firm; station-3; length-2cm; and cervical dilatation: 1-2 cm. What is Thembi's Bishop Score?
questions.rationale: Per Myles Textbook for Midwives Bishop scoring: dilatation 1-2 cm = 1, length/effacement 2 cm (0-1 cm effaced) = 1, station -3 = 0, consistency firm = 0, position mid = 1, giving a total of 3.

questions.stem: The multiplier is 1000 and the denominator is live births in the same year. 184. Some principles of time management include:-
questions.option_a: Priority setting, evaluating progress, minimal breaks
questions.option_c: Avoiding delegation, Time analysis, controlling interruptions

questions.rationale: Per nursing management/leadership principles, effective time management includes time analysis, goal/priority setting and delegation. Options advocating 'avoiding delegation' or 'minimal breaks' are contrary to sound time management.

questions.stem: A type of educational assessment which is generally carried out throughout a course or project is
questions.rationale: Formative assessment is conducted throughout a course to monitor learning and give feedback, whereas summative assessment occurs at the end; standard educational assessment principle.

questions.stem: which of the following is the advantage of integration of services
questions.option_a: save time and money for the nurse
questions.option_c: patients are integrated in the approach
questions.option_d: there is high chance of cross infection between sick and health especially children
questions.rationale: Integration of services allows a client to receive several services in one visit, saving time and resources for both client and provider and reducing missed opportunities; cross-infection risk is a disadvantage, not an advantage.

questions.stem: The anterior posterior fontanelle normally close by the age of;
questions.rationale: The posterior fontanelle closes at approximately 6-8 weeks and the anterior fontanelle closes at approximately 18 months. Option C (18 months and 6 weeks) correctly states these respective closure ages. (Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols; standard paediatric texts.)

questions.stem: In enterobiasis infection, the adult worm lives in the:-
questions.rationale: Per parasitology in Kenyan nursing texts, in enterobiasis the adult Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) lives in the caecum and appendiceal region; females migrate to the perianal area to lay eggs. Caecum is the specific site making it the best answer over 'large intestines'.

questions.stem: The primary purpose of conducting an epidemiologic investigation is to:
questions.option_a: Identify groups who are at risk of contracting the disease
questions.option_b: Identify geographical location of cases in the community
questions.option_c: Delineate the aetiology of the epidemic
questions.option_d: Encourage cooperation and support of the community
questions.rationale: The primary purpose of an epidemiologic investigation is to delineate the aetiology of the epidemic to guide control (epidemiology principles).

questions.stem: Communicable disease control measures at individual and village level include:-
questions.option_c: Completing immunisation, protection of springs and wells
questions.option_d: Participate in vector and reservoir control, immunisation coverage
questions.rationale: Individual/village level: completing immunisation and protecting springs/wells (MOH Kenya community health guidelines).

questions.stem: A mother delivers a baby who has an Apgar score of 0/1. Which of the following findings demonstrate that Apgar score:
questions.option_b: Neonatal fetal heart rate of less than100
questions.option_d: The body and the extremities are pale
questions.rationale: An Apgar of 0/1 indicates a severely depressed neonate; only the completely pale/absent colour (0 for colour, no cyanosis grading possible) fits. Minimal grimace, HR<100 and gasping respiration all score 1 in their categories and would raise the score above near-zero, whereas generalised pallor reflects the profoundly depressed state. Per Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols (Apgar scoring). ⚠ More than one defensible answer

questions.stem: The learning domain concerned with acquisition of facts, concepts and principles is:
questions.rationale: Cognitive domain (Bloom's taxonomy): acquisition of facts, concepts and principles.

questions.stem: Maslow's hierarchy of needs in correct ascending sequence is:
questions.rationale: Maslow's hierarchy guides nursing prioritisation; nurses address lower-order physiological and safety needs before higher-order psychosocial needs (nursing theory; leadership texts).

questions.stem: The predilection of HIV for certain cells in the immune system results in
questions.option_a: More T4 lymphocytes and general lymphocytopenia
questions.option_d: Susceptibility to opportunistic infection and neoplasm
questions.rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth and Kenya HIV guidelines, HIV targets CD4 (T4) helper lymphocytes causing their depletion and immunosuppression, leading to opportunistic infections and neoplasms.

questions.stem: The nurse is aware that the most common assessment finding in a child with ulcerative colitis is:
questions.rationale: Per paediatric med-surg nursing, the most common presenting finding in ulcerative colitis is profuse (often bloody) diarrhea. Abdominal cramps and distention occur but diarrhea is the hallmark assessment finding.

questions.stem: The health messages that should be shared with a patient who has suffered from myocardial infarction include:
questions.option_a: Eating a low-salt but fluid-free diet
questions.option_c: Reporting to healthcare providers if extremely fatigued
questions.option_d: Identification and modification of all risk factors
questions.rationale: Brunner & Suddarth cardiac rehabilitation: post-MI teaching centres on identification and modification of all modifiable risk factors.

questions.stem: Bell’s palsy involves the following cranial nerve
questions.rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, Bell's palsy is an acute peripheral paralysis of cranial nerve VII (facial nerve), causing unilateral facial weakness.

questions.stem: Which of the following should be included in the health teachings among clients receiving Valium:
questions.option_a: Avoid taking CNS depressant like alcohol.
questions.option_b: There are no restrictions in activities.
questions.option_d: Any beverage like coffee may be taken
questions.rationale: Valium (diazepam) is a benzodiazepine CNS depressant. Combining it with alcohol or other CNS depressants causes dangerous additive/synergistic sedation and respiratory depression. Clients must be instructed to avoid alcohol strictly. Activities requiring alertness (driving, operating machinery) should also be restricted. (Kenya EML; BNF pharmacology; Brunner & Suddarth's.)

questions.stem: The trophoblast cells of the developing zygote from the:-
questions.rationale: Per Myles Textbook for Midwives, the trophoblast (outer cells of the blastocyst) develops into the chorion and the fetal portion of the placenta; the inner cell mass forms the fetus and amnion.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not the purpose of assessment?
questions.rationale: Purposes of assessment include certification, safeguarding the public, and monitoring the program; safeguarding the educational institution is not a legitimate purpose, making it the exception. Educational assessment principles.

questions.stem: Which syndrome mimics anaphylactic shock?
questions.rationale: Acute angioedema presents similarly to anaphylaxis; differentiating the two requires careful history and assessment. Management with epinephrine is common to both (Brunner & Suddarth; clinical reasoning).

questions.stem: What is the term for the clear, gel-like substance that fills the space between the lens and retina in the eye?
questions.rationale: Vitreous detachment causes floaters; vitreous haemorrhage (diabetic retinopathy) causes sudden vision loss. BScN nurses recognise flashes + floaters as a retinal detachment warning and advise same-day ophthalmology referral (anatomy; Brunner & Suddarth; ophthalmology).
